svg.title: Sensors node wiring
svg.desc: ESP32 DevKit top view with three breadboard rails: 5 V from VIN, 3.3 V from 3V3, and GND. MQ-5 module: VCC to 5 V, GND to GND, AO through a 10 k resistor to GPIO 34, with a second 10 k resistor from GPIO 34 to GND; DO unused. Flame sensor: VCC to 3.3 V, GND, DO to GPIO 35. HC-SR501: VCC to 5 V, GND, OUT to GPIO 32.
svg.text: Kitchen. MQ-5 methane sensor and flame sensor by the stove; the PIR watches the back door.
Divider: halves AO (up to 5 V) to ≤ 2.5 V for GPIO 34
Pin order varies: read the labels under the dome.
USB 5 V (≥ 1 A charger: the MQ-5 heater draws ~150 mA)
5 V rail from VIN (only while the board is on USB): MQ-5 and PIR.
3.3 V rail from 3V3: flame sensor, so its DO stays 3.3 V.
GND rail: every module's GND and the lower 10 kΩ resistor.
Gets hot: keep it off plastic. A new one needs 24–48 h
powered to settle, then press Calibrate in clean air.
HomeShield ignores it for 90 s after each power-up.
Sensors page: set its output wiring to 10 kΩ + 10 kΩ.
Mount it high: methane is lighter than air.
Flame: turn its screw until its LED lights only for a
lighter flame ~30 cm away. DO goes LOW on a flame:
keep “Active when the pin is LOW” ticked.
PIR: jumper on H (repeat), time screw fully anticlockwise
(~3 s), sensitivity in the middle. Settles in ~1 min.
